statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.380, s.452 and s.404 (charged); IPC s.302 and s.404 convictions upheld
weapon: Licensed revolver (recovered with live and spent cartridges)
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence, including mobile IMEI/SIM call records (scientific/documentary), recovery of revolver and handset, recovery memos, oral testimony of witnesses, and a bank deposit
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC (life imprisonment and Rs.50,000 fine) and s.404 IPC (3 years RI and Rs.5,000 fine); acquitted of s.380 and s.452 IPC; sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed on merits; conviction upheld; default imprisonment in lieu of fine under s.302 reduced from three years to six months
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302) and criminal misappropriation-type offence under IPC s.404
neutral_facts: The victim was found dead inside a house in Delhi, having suffered bullet injuries to the left side of the temporal region and the left side of the abdomen. Police received a telephone call about the body on the evening of 23 July 2005. The victim's wife, who had been in Chandigarh, stated that the victim had left Chandigarh for Delhi carrying a licensed revolver, a mobile phone SIM and a sum of Rs. 3 lakhs intended for negotiating a settlement. The sum was not fully recovered. Records showed that the victim's SIM became inactive on the date of the murder and that two incoming calls from a Chandigarh telephone had been received on that day. Investigators then found that a handset bearing a particular IMEI number, which had been used with the victim's SIM, was used with a SIM registered in the name of the accused, immediately after the murder and until 2 August 2005. Service provider records confirmed the registration of that SIM in the accused's name. Police recovered three mobile handsets from the accused, one bearing the IMEI number of the victim's handset, and a revolver with live and spent cartridges that had belonged to the victim. Recovery memos bore the signatures of the accused's brother and father, who later asserted that their signatures had been taken on blank papers. The accused was arrested on 6 August 2005. A deposit of Rs. 9,000 had been made into a bank account in the accused's name two days after the murder.
physical_harm: Death from bullet injuries to the left temporal region and left abdomen
number_of_offences: 4 charged (ss.302, 380, 452, 404 IPC); 2 finally upheld (ss.302 and 404 IPC)
financial_property_loss: Rs. 3 lakhs not recovered (per wife's statement); Rs. 9,000 deposit in the accused's bank account two days after the murder; the victim's mobile handset and licensed revolver also taken
key_evidence_accepted: IMEI/SIM call records showing the victim's handset used with the accused's SIM immediately after the murder; nodal officer evidence (PW22) on SIM registration; recovery of the revolver with cartridges and of the handset from the accused; recovery memos authenticated by signatures of the accused's brother and father; continued use of the SIM until arrest
witness_credibility: The Court accepted that the wife's (PW23) statement contained a discrepancy about the direction of calls but held it insignificant against scientific IMEI/SIM evidence. The brother (PW12) and father (PW13) denied signing the recovery memos, but neither disputed the authenticity of their signatures, so the Court held the signatures genuine.
post_offence_conduct: Immediately after the murder, the accused used the victim's handset with the accused's own registered SIM and continued using that SIM until arrest; the accused was in possession of the victim's handset and revolver
custody_duration: Arrested 6 August 2005; total custody duration not stated
trial_duration: offence: 23.7.2005; trial judgment: 21.4.2008; High Court: 18.3.2009; Supreme Court: 22.09.2011
legal_representation: Accused: Sanjay K. Agarwal. State: J.S. Attri, P.K. Dey and Sadhna Sandhu (for Anil Katiyar)
investigation_status: FIR registered (No. 297 of 2005, Police Station Krishna Nagar, on 7.1.2006); investigation led to arrest; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302 and 404 IPC, acquitted under ss.380 and 452 IPC. High Court: appeal dismissed on merits; default sentence reduced to six months. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed; conviction upheld.
defence_argument: (1) The accused was implicated through a fabricated story, since the handset was traced via the victim's wife's disclosure and a discrepancy existed in her call timing evidence, so the handset recovery was a concoction; (2) the recovery witnesses (brother and father) said their signatures were obtained on blank papers; (3) the Rs. 9,000 deposit did not connect the accused to the crime
legal_principle_applied: Every mobile handset has a unique IMEI number recorded by service providers, so IMEI/SIM call records are conclusive scientific evidence that can outweigh discrepancies in oral evidence; recovery memo signatures not disputed by signatories are treated as authentic
